method: Read _brief.md, rubric/jury.md, rubric/critic.md, team/taste.md. Per ref, in brief order: desktop-fold, mobile-fold, desktop-overlay, mobile-overlay, sheet-desktop, sheet-mobile, page-text.txt, evidence.json (outline, motion, reducedMotion, idleNavigation, overlaysDismissed), motion-sheet.png, report.json (all viewports). Single screenshots opened to check doubts: ref-0007/desktop-page-03.png (is the Swehl School heading visible above the video cards? it is not); ref-0008/desktop-page-02.png (what fills the dark band after the hero? nothing visible), ref-0008/desktop-page-04.png (copy and claims in the coral 'silos' section), ref-0008/desktop-page-05.png (journey cards: is the body copy visible? no, front faces only; section heading sits under the header), ref-0008/desktop-page-09.png (Centaur human+AI diagram). No browser opened. Not verified: (a) whether the Swehl hero normally plays a video. report.json logs 'The element has no supported sources' twice, and the hero is a blurred tan field, so a video that failed to load in the capture is an inference only; (b) whether Swehl's 'SWEHL SCHOOL / YOUR #1 RESOURCE...' heading is hidden by a scroll reveal on desktop (missing in desktop-page-03, present in motion-sheet frame 07-scroll-2250px); (c) what the fixed dice icon on Swehl does; (d) whether Resolute's three value lines ('Hyper-Personalised Health Plans...', 'Built on Diagnostics, Not Guesswork', 'One Size Fits You...') ever become readable in a real scroll (the navy band in desktop-page-02 is empty; only a faint fragment shows in mobile-page-02); (e) smoothness of any motion, which stills cannot show; (f) Resolute prices (none on the page) and what 'Get Your Blueprint' costs or leads to.

ref-0007.business: Inference: Swehl is a US direct-to-consumer brand that sells breastfeeding kits and accessories ($22 to $99.99) to expecting and new parents, using free education (Swehl School videos) and community chats (Swehl Circles) to recruit buyers. Paying action, inferred: buy a kit ('SHOP KITS'); the email + due-date sign-up is lead capture for lifecycle marketing (inference). Whether Circles are paid is unverified.

reasons.story: Voice is the strongest asset: the copy sounds like a frank peer, not a brochure ('Quick relief for chapped and sore nips', 'Breastfeeding Positions - Because Options.', 'Partners are People, Too.', 'Real Talk', 'hype up & hang', mobile pop-up 'on the reg'; page-text.txt). The hero gives one readable line ('BREASTFEEDING TOOLS MADE FOR THIS CENTURY', H1 at 7%). But the page is a three-pillar storefront (shop, school, circles; announced by the marquee H2s at 19%), not an argument: there is no problem beat (the customer's pain, overwhelm and sore nipples, appears only in a product subline and in the third testimonial), and 'made for this century' sets up an old-way-vs-new contrast the page never shows. Sequence breaks: (1) the first beat is interrupted by a newsletter pop-up about 1 s after load (motion-sheet 02-load-1000ms; desktop-fold and mobile-overlay) that covers the H1, so the first ask comes before the message; (2) the shop beat dead-ends: all three products are 'SOLD OUT' (page-text.txt), so the hero's promise of tools leads to a wall; (3) the proof (testimonials + Forbes/Fast Company/Vogue/Glamour) backs the education and community ('empowered by the knowledge', 'the Swehl community and educational info'), not the products the hero sells. The visual concept partly serves the message: warm, staged photos of diverse parents with babies (desktop-page-03) say 'made by and for parents'; the recurring arch shape (pop-up arc, 'LET'S TALK IT OUT' set on an arch over a group photo) carries the brand's softness. The hero itself shows no parent, product or tool, only a blurred colour field (desktop-fold; see method (a)). Calibrated: above generic because of voice and a clear three-pillar map; held at 6 by the missing problem beat, the sold-out shop and proof aimed at the wrong pillar.

beats.beat: 0. Pop-up (about 1 s after load): 'GET CUSTOMIZED CONTENT IN YOUR INBOX.' email + due/birth date, covers the H1
beats.job: Ask before any message. Breaks the opening

beats.beat: 1. Announcement bar: 'So nice The New York Times wrote about us (thrice)'
beats.job: Proof first, in the brand's playful voice. Works

beats.beat: 2. Hero: 'BREASTFEEDING TOOLS MADE FOR THIS CENTURY' + SHOP KITS / GET EDUCATED (mobile screenshot reads 'LET'S LEARN')
beats.job: Promise + two paths. No pain stated, no tool shown
beats.evidence: mobile-fold.png, outline H1 7%, actions firstScreen true

beats.beat: 3. Marquee: expert-led video tutorials, virtual talk circles, made by parents & docs
beats.job: Table of contents for the three pillars; also a credibility line ('parents & docs')

beats.beat: 4. Shop: 'BREASTFEEDING ESSENTIALS', Latch Kit $99.99, Cloud 9 $65, Nips Duo $22, all SOLD OUT
beats.job: Delivers the hero's promise, then dead-ends

beats.beat: 5. Swehl School: 'YOUR #1 RESOURCE FOR PREGNANCY AND BEYOND.' 75+ videos, video card carousel
beats.job: Second pillar; strongest customer-voice titles

beats.beat: 6. Swehl Circles: 'LET'S TALK IT OUT', digital expert-led community chats
beats.job: Third pillar; best section design (arch over real group photo)

beats.beat: 7. Three testimonials (5 stars), Hannah A / Amy S / Sarah Z
beats.job: Proof, but about learning and community, not the products

beats.beat: 8. Press logos: Forbes, Fast Company, Vogue, Glamour
beats.job: Second proof beat, repeats the announcement bar's job

beats.beat: 9. Footer newsletter: 'Get newsletters that are made for you at every step of your journey.'
beats.job: Closes on the same lead-capture ask as the pop-up, not on a purchase

claims.verdict: confirmed with correction (outside my criterion; story angle only)
claims.evidence: Each pillar gets its own flat background: lilac (bar/pop-up), blue (shop), orange (school), yellow (circles/testimonials), brown (footer); colour works as chapter markers, which helps the three-pillar map. 'Simple' is relative: report.json counts 6 chromatic colours and 7 background colours on desktop. Roles are clear, the count is not small.

claims.claim: 2. Very balanced play of text sizes
claims.evidence: There is a decisive jump from display (100/94/70 px, Caslon Rounded, 6% of text) to body (Roobert 94%), so headlines lead. But report.json flags 9 font sizes on desktop (WARN too-many-font-sizes, aim 5). 'Clear hierarchy' is accurate; 'balanced' undersells that the display size dominates on purpose. Contrast of the H1 is 2.0-2.2:1 on all viewports (FAIL), so the main message line is hard to read on screen.

evidence.json motion: no scroll libraries (gsap, scrollTrigger, lenis, locomotive all false), only CSS transitions of 300-900 ms (carousel transforms, colour changes, one opacity reveal near y=3600), scriptDrivenOnScroll 2. The page scrolls as ordinary stacked sections (sheet-desktop). What is distinctive is section design, not scrolling: the arch shapes and the curved 'LET'S TALK IT OUT' heading. Correct term: 'distinctive section shapes (arches) and colour-coded chapters', not a scrolling concept. Scrolling does not carry the story here; section order and colour do.

claims.claim: 4. CTA early on, fixed at the bottom, with a circular radius
claims.evidence: Early: confirmed, SHOP KITS and GET EDUCATED are on the first screen (actions firstAt 11%, firstScreen true; mobile-fold.png). Fixed at the bottom: contested, every action in evidence.json has sticky:false. The element fixed at bottom-right of every screen is a dice icon with no label (function unverified), and the orange arrow at the bottom of mobile-fold is a scroll cue, not an action. Radius: the buttons are pills (radius 9999px in report.json), i.e. fully rounded ends, not circles. Story note: the first ask the visitor actually meets is the newsletter pop-up (~1 s), not the CTA.

problems: No problem beat and no 'old way' shown: 'made for this century' promises a contrast the page never draws; the customer's pain (overwhelm, sore nipples, giving up) only surfaces in a product subline and the third testimonial (page-text.txt). Smallest fix: one short section after the hero naming the 2-3 pains in the customer's words, each mapped to a tool or a video.

The opening is interrupted and the paying path dead-ends: the newsletter pop-up covers the H1 about 1 s after load (motion-sheet 02-load-1000ms), and every product in the shop beat is SOLD OUT (page-text.txt). The story's first promise leads to a wall. Fix: delay the pop-up until after the shop beat or exit intent; when stock is out, turn the shop beat into 'join the restock list' so the beat still has a next step.

Proof backs the wrong pillar: testimonials praise knowledge and community, not the kits the hero sells, and no proof sits next to the products. Fix: one product-specific quote or outcome under the Latch Kit, and move the press logos up next to the hero claim instead of repeating the announcement bar's job at the end.
keep: Customer-voice copy: frank, warm, slightly irreverent titles ('Partners are People, Too.', 'Because Options.', 'nips') that sound like a friend who has been there; function: lowers the embarrassment barrier of an intimate topic.

Marquee as table of contents ('expert-led video tutorials • virtual talk circles • made by parents & docs') right after the hero; function: tells the visitor the page's three chapters before they scroll. Mark the copies aria-hidden so screen readers do not hear 12 H2s.
Colour-coded chapters (one flat background per pillar) plus a recurring arch shape; function: the visitor always knows which part of the offer they are in.

ref-0008.business: Inference: Resolute (Applied Healthspan Private Limited, India; +91 phone) sells a personalised preventive-health / longevity programme: diagnostics (85+ biomarkers, optional MRI), a doctor + coach + AI 'Centaur team', a 100-day framework and six goal journeys (fat loss, gut, running, cognition, longevity, total body), plus side offers (Supp[RX] supplements, aging test, workplace plans). Audience, inferred from testimonials: affluent self-optimisers, founders and athletes. Paying action, inferred: 'Get Your Blueprint' (start the programme); no price anywhere (evidence.json prices: []).

reasons.story: The skeleton is a textbook argument and is the stronger structure of the two: promise (H1 'More Healthy Years. Built With You.' + doctors-and-AI mechanism, 1%) > problem ('Tired of one-size-fits-all health hacks?... fragmented, scattered, and generic', desktop-page-02) > answer ('Your health doesn't live in silos. Neither do we.', desktop-page-04) > offer range (six journeys, 32%) > how it works in three steps (38-50%) > who does it (human + AI, 55%) > proof (65%) > team (73%) > objections (FAQ, 87%) > close (94%). The main CTA label 'Get Your Blueprint' is step 2 of 'How it Works', so the ask and the process share one word; that is good message-house discipline. It loses points on three things. (1) Brochure voice: the company's coined terms replace the customer's words ('Human 360 - Body Data Stack', 'Whole of Me Construct', 'Cognitive Connectone', 'Adiposity Atlas', 'Centaur Team', 'Hyper-Personalised'); the only customer voice is in the testimonials, which are good and specific ('I was able to follow about 70-80% of their suggestions'). (2) Scroll design hides beats instead of carrying them: the three value lines (H3 at 7%) do not show in the desktop or mobile captures (navy band empty in desktop-page-02); report.json flags hidden-content FAIL (1 element on desktop, 11 on tablet and mobile, including the Centaur role descriptions); journey descriptions sit on the back of flip cards (motion sample slide_content_back) and the section heading 'From risk reversal, to high performance' is under the header in desktop-page-05; layout shift 1.73. (3) The offer's shape arrives late and competes: '100-day' appears first in the FAQ and the close; the persistent promo bar sells a different product (Supp[RX] 'Reveal Your Stack') on every screen; 'Outcomes, Not Promises' is claimed but no outcome figure is shown, only '10,000+ Personalised Journeys' and four quotes; Guides & Blogs sits between team and FAQ by habit. Visual concept: the lone hiker on a summit (hero) and the iridescent head (silos) are generic wellness metaphors; the human-expert vs AI-copilot diagram meeting at 'Safe, expert-approved care decisions' (desktop-page-09) is the one visual that states the actual mechanism.

beats.beat: 0. Promo bar on every screen: 'LIVE NOW Supp[RX]... Confused about what supplements to take? We can help.' + 'Reveal Your Stack'
beats.job: Second, competing offer before and during the main story
beats.evidence: desktop-fold.png, all sheet pages, actions sticky true

beats.beat: 1. Hero: 'More Healthy Years. Built With You.' + 'guided by doctors and powered by AI' + Get Your Blueprint (header)
beats.job: Promise + mechanism. Clear

beats.beat: 2. Dark band: three value lines (personalised plans, diagnostics not guesswork, one size fits you)
beats.job: Differentiators, but not visible in captures
beats.evidence: outline H3 7%; desktop-page-02.png empty band; mobile-page-02 fragment

beats.beat: 3. Problem: 'Tired of one-size-fits-all health hacks? ... fragmented, scattered, and generic.'
beats.job: Names the enemy. Generic phrasing ('health hacks')

beats.beat: 4. Answer: 'Welcome to What Your Health Can Be' / 'Your health doesn't live in silos. Neither do we.' + Clarity not Overwhelm / Blueprints not Band-Aids / Outcomes not Promises

beats.beat: 5. Offer range: 'From risk reversal, to high performance', six branded journeys on fanned flip cards
beats.job: Lets visitors find their goal; descriptions behind the flip

beats.beat: 6. Outcome marquee: Improved Metabolic Function... Improved Cognition & Mood (infinite loop)
beats.job: List of outcomes as decoration, no numbers

beats.job: Process; the CTA word comes from step 2

beats.job: Proof in customer voice; 10,000+ unsupported elsewhere

beats.beat: 10. 'Not just a system - real care, from a team...': doctors and coaches with titles; 'We help you add more disease-free, high-performing years'
beats.job: Authority; restates the hero promise

beats.beat: 11. Guides & Blogs (4 articles)
beats.job: There by habit; breaks the run from trust to objections

beats.beat: 12. FAQs (8 questions incl. 'Why 100 days?')
beats.job: Objections; introduces the 100-day format for the first time

beats.beat: 13. Close: 'Start your 100-day health transformation today. Powered by your data, guided by experts.' + Get Your Blueprint

claims.claim: 1. Every section is packaged with good scrolling
claims.evidence: Scroll machinery is real: evidence.json libraries gsap, scrollTrigger, splitText, lenis (smoothed scroll) and lottie all true; scriptDrivenOnScroll 13. But 'every section' is wrong: Guides & Blogs, FAQ and footer are plain blocks (sheet-desktop pages 12-14). And 'good' does not hold for the story: scroll-driven content does not always arrive. report.json hidden-content FAIL (desktop 1, tablet/mobile 11 elements never visible during a full scroll, including 'designed for the life you're meant to live' and the Centaur role descriptions); the three value lines are invisible in the captures (desktop-page-02.png); layout shift 1.73 (FAIL, limit 0.25); reducedMotion still has 14 elements moving on scroll and 4 without input; 58 infinite text loops with no pause control. Under the team's Never rule (content that only appears through animation), part of this is a defect, not a strength.

This is one long page (pageHeight 13022), so these are section-to-section transitions, not page transitions (viewTransitions false; idleNavigation null). Lenis is present, which suggests smoothed scrolling, but smoothness cannot be judged from stills; the motion juror should rule. Counter-evidence for 'smooth': layout shift 1.73 in report.json. Story angle: background colour changes (navy > white > coral > cream > burgundy > white > cream > burgundy) mark chapters clearly in sheet-desktop.

claims.claim: 3. Every section has a unique design
claims.evidence: True for the first ~60% of the page: photo hero, arrows-and-statement problem, coral iridescent head with claim pills, fanned flip cards, outcome marquee, burgundy sticky steps, human/AI diagram (sheet-desktop pages 01-09). From testimonials on, sections are conventional cards, team row, blog grid and accordion (pages 10-14). Story caution: unique-per-section design without a recurring visual motif means the design does not repeat the one message; the visual idea changes with every chapter while the copy changes vocabulary (Blueprint, Journey, Stack, Construct, Atlas) as well.

problems: Key beats depend on scroll animation that does not reliably show them: the three differentiators after the hero are not visible in the captures (desktop-page-02.png), 1-11 elements are flagged hidden-content FAIL (report.json), and each journey's description sits on the back of a flip card (desktop-page-05.png). The story's argument has holes exactly where the motion is. Fix: render all copy statically and let motion only enhance it; show one line of each journey's outcome on the card front.

Brochure vocabulary instead of the customer's words: coined product terms (Human 360 Body Data Stack, Whole of Me Construct, Cognitive Connectone, Adiposity Atlas, Centaur Team, Precision Wellness Stacks) carry the explanation, and 'Outcomes, Not Promises' is never backed by a single outcome figure. Fix: rewrite each step and journey as 'you get X, measured by Y' in plain words, and put one measured result (e.g. biomarker change after 100 days) next to the 10,000+ claim.

The offer has no stable shape until the end and competes with itself: '100-day' first appears in the FAQ and the close, no price or 'what it costs' anywhere (prices []), and a promo bar for a different product (Supp[RX]) runs on every screen. Fix: state 'a 100-day programme: tests, doctor-led blueprint, coaching' in the hero subline, put price or starting price by 'Get Your Blueprint' (team Always rule), and drop the competing bar on this page or turn it into a link in the journeys section. Cut or move Guides & Blogs below the FAQ.
keep: Problem > reframe pairing: 'Tired of one-size-fits-all health hacks?' followed by 'Your health doesn't live in silos. Neither do we.'; function: names the enemy, then positions the brand against it in one memorable line.
CTA wording that is also a named step of the process ('Get Your Blueprint' = How it Works step 2); function: the visitor knows exactly where the button puts them in the journey.

Mechanism diagram: human expert and AI copilot as two fields meeting at 'Safe, expert-approved care decisions' (desktop-page-09.png); function: shows how the service works and answers the trust question about AI in one picture. Needs its role texts rendered without relying on a reveal.
